# wakeci

wakeci is a CI server: jobs are YAML files, and each run of a job is a build
with a numeric ID. This page tells agents and scripts how to use its API.

## Authenticate

Send an API key: `Authorization: Bearer wk_...`. A key has scopes (read,
run, write) on all jobs or on some jobs, and only sees those jobs.
`GET /api/whoami` says what the key may do and which server answers.

401 means the key is missing, wrong or expired. 403 means the key may not
do that, or not on that job. 404 means no such route or build. 429 means
too many requests: wait `Retry-After` seconds.

## Use MCP if you can

`POST /mcp` serves the API as MCP tools (Streamable HTTP, stateless) with
the same key: whoami, list_jobs, find_builds, build_summary, read_log,
read_artifact, run_job, abort_build.

## Why did a build fail?

`GET /api/build/<id>/summary` returns the status, the tasks, the artifacts,
the summary the job wrote (jobSummary) and the last 100 lines (tail=N) of
each task that failed, timed out or was aborted. For more of a log:
`GET /api/build/<id>/log/<task>?grep=FAILED` or `?tail=500`.

A build page URL such as `https://<host>/build/123` has the build ID 123;
its API is `/api/build/123`. Build IDs belong to one server: `whoami` gives
the range of IDs a server has. Ask the server in the URL.

## Wait for a build

`GET /api/build/<id>?wait=300` (or `/summary?wait=300`) answers as soon as
the build ends, or after 300 seconds; repeat until its status is finished,
failed, aborted or timed out. Don't poll in a loop.

## Find builds

`GET /api/feed` returns builds newest first: `job=<name>` and
`status=failed` match exactly, `q=` searches words, `limit=` up to 200.
To follow new builds, keep the newest ID you have and ask for
`?after=<id>&limit=200`; page back with `before=<oldest id>`. Send the
`ETag` back as `If-None-Match` to get 304 when nothing changed.

## Logs and artifacts

`GET /api/build/<id>` lists each task's log URL (`tasks[].log`, absent if
the task wrote none) and each artifact's URL (`build_artifacts[].url`). Use
these URLs instead of building paths. Files support `Range`, for example
`Range: bytes=-65536` for the end of a log.

## Run and abort

`POST /api/job/<name>/run` with the job's parameters as form fields returns
the new build ID (run scope). Parameters can't reference secrets or
contain quotes or line breaks. `POST /api/build/<id>/abort` aborts it.

## Everything else

The OpenAPI (Swagger 2.0) spec of every route is at `/docs/swagger.json`,
and `/docs/mcp.json` lists the MCP tools with the scope each needs; both
need no key. People read the same spec at `/docs/api/`.
